clue.text: Order given to old shock trooper

parts.note: to order someone is to command them

explanation.surface: An instruction is handed to a veteran soldier of an elite assault unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier trained for surprise raids, a classic shock trooper.

clue.text: Bonds issued by retailing groups

explanation.surface: Securities are put out by groups of shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Chains are fetters that bind, and also groups of shops under one owner, such as supermarket brands.

clue.text: A brave doctor, and certainly no dove

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
in politics a hawk favours war, the opposite of a peace-loving dove

explanation.surface: A courageous medic, definitely not a pacifist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A brave' looks like an adjective, but a brave is a Native American warrior, and the Mohawk are a Native American people.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mohawk warrior is a brave, the old term for a Native American fighting man.

clue.text: Recompense when the afternoon begins

explanation.surface: Compensation is due the moment the clock passes noon.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: the afternoon starts when the a.m. (morning) ends, so read the answer as AM ENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends is to offer compensation; and noon is the moment the morning period, a.m., is over.

clue.text: Cleaning lady has to practise Buddhist exercises

parts.note: a daily is British slang for a cleaner who comes in each day
to do something is to carry it out or practise it
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A cleaner must take up meditation alongside her chores.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily dozen is a routine of morning physical exercises.

clue.text: Coming to get commercial air-extractor

parts.note: a TV commercial is an ad
a vent lets stale air out

explanation.surface: Someone arrives to collect an extractor fan from a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means an arrival, especially the coming of Christ celebrated before Christmas.

clue.text: No compensation is offered for battle fatalities

explanation.surface: Families of those killed in war receive nothing in payment.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: those killed are the dead, a loss to the army.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead loss is a total loss with nothing recovered; and soldiers killed are dead, a loss to their side.

clue.text: A German gets stumped by a German physicist

parts.note: ein is German for a, the indefinite article
st is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped
again ein, the German word for a

explanation.surface: A German cricketer is stumped by another German, a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter is 'stumped' when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while they are out of their ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein was the German-born physicist behind relativity.

clue.text: Record Wagnerian operas with a finer ending

parts.note: to tape something is to record it
the Ring is Wagner's cycle of four operas

explanation.surface: Someone records the Ring cycle so it closes more delicately.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tapering narrows gradually towards a thin point at one end.

clue.text: A wild cat lithe and muscular

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the letters of the two following words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A wild feline, supple and powerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletic describes a strong, well-built, muscular physique.

clue.text: Herb and Tom bite

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a nip is a small bite

explanation.surface: Herb and Tom, two men, take a bite.
explanation.walkthrough: Herb and Tom look like two men's names; Herb is the definition and Tom gives the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Catnip is an aromatic plant of the mint family that cats love.

clue.text: Don's away for a break at present

indicators.note: a break breaks the words up, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the phrase, with the S of the possessive kept

explanation.surface: The university lecturer is off on holiday right now.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a British university lecturer; the anagram uses every letter of DONS AWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays means in the current era, these days.

clue.text: Seconds afterwards he could be out on the tiles

definitions.text: he could be out on the tiles

parts.note: later means afterwards

explanation.surface: Moments later a man goes out on the town all night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out on the tiles' is British slang for a night of partying; here it is literal: a roofer working on tiles.
explanation.definitionFit: A slater lays slates or tiles on roofs, so he works up on the tiles.

clue.text: One member taking the Community line is exemplary

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
an MP is a Member of Parliament
EC stands for the European Community
a cable is a line, as in a telephone line

explanation.surface: An MP who toes the European party line is a model of good conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Impeccable means faultless, beyond reproach, so a model to follow.

clue.text: Trainee chef is put back on duty

parts.note: a commis is a junior chef in a professional kitchen

indicators.note: putting a word back turns it round, so the word is is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A kitchen apprentice is returned to his shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses IS to give SI.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission is a task or duty entrusted to someone.

clue.text: Young nobleman consumed the whole vegetable

indicators.note: the first word has swallowed the next, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a scion is a young descendant of a noble family
all means the whole

explanation.surface: A young aristocrat ate an entire vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallion is a spring onion, a mild green vegetable.

clue.text: Detect how to breathe in the open air

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Detect how to breathe in the open air' (5,3): SNUFF (breathe in) + OUT (in the open air) is clear, but 'Detect' cannot define SNUFF OUT (extinguish); likely an OCR misread that no search confirmed.
annotationWithheld.clue: Detect how to breathe in the open air

clue.text: Cadger is rightly put to shame

indicators.note: putting the letters right means arranging them properly, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A scrounger is deservedly humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rightly put' rearranges CADGER and IS; a cadger is someone who scrounges.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgrace is the loss of respect that brings shame on someone.

clue.text: Am I not permitted to obtain purchase of a girder?

parts.note: the question 'can't I?' asks whether I am not allowed
a lever gives purchase, the grip that lets a force move a load

explanation.surface: A puzzled builder asks whether he may buy a steel beam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' looks like buying, but here it means mechanical grip, which a lever provides.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a projecting beam or girder fixed at only one end.

clue.text: Arrange to get a clothes-drier erected

parts.note: a washing line is used to dry clothes
something erected is put up

explanation.surface: Someone plans to have a washing line put up.
explanation.definitionFit: To line up things is to set them in order or arrange them.

clue.text: You and I declare that he's a man of the cloth

parts.note: you and I together are we
to aver is to declare firmly

explanation.surface: We state that he is a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man of the cloth' normally means a priest; here it is literal, a man who makes cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A weaver makes fabric on a loom, so he is literally a man of the cloth.

clue.text: Stalwart is right to be absorbed in academic work

indicators.note: one piece is soaked up inside the other

parts.note: study is academic work

explanation.surface: A loyal supporter rightly loses himself in his research.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy and stalwart both mean strong and robust.

clue.text: Socialist energy must be released

parts.note: socialists are on the political left
go means energy or vigour, as in 'full of go'

explanation.surface: Left-wing vigour must be set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To have let go of something is to have released one's hold on it.

clue.text: Mishap resulting from one day in ambience of stress

indicators.note: one piece sits within the surroundings of another

parts.note: accent is stress placed on a syllable
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A mishap caused by a single day in a stressful atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stress' suggests tension, but it means accent, the emphasis on a syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unlucky, unplanned mishap.

clue.text: A pressure line it is, and nothing but

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing
bar means except, as does but

explanation.surface: A weather line, that's what it is, and nothing more.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: He views an outside broadcast by priest's assistant

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for an outside broadcast
a server assists the priest at Mass

explanation.surface: A TV broadcast from outside is staffed by an altar helper.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer is someone who watches or looks on.

clue.text: Final pay received by a woman is lower

parts.note: net pay is what remains after deductions
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman's take-home pay is less.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower or under, as in the nether regions.

clue.text: Jo prayed to be free from danger

indicators.note: letters set free from their order can fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Jo prays to be spared from peril.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeopardy is the state of being in peril or at risk.
